evidence: Wikipedia's article on 'Genius of Love': Grandmaster Flash and the Furious Five's 'It's Nasty (Genius of Love)' (Sugar Hill, 1982) was re-recorded by a live band, an interpolation rather than a sample of the original recording, as was the usual practice then. Dr. Jeckyll & Mr. Hyde's 'Genius Rap' (1981) used it earlier. Typed as sample to match the map's other interpolation edges (e-kraftwerk-planetrock).

trackPair.whatToListenFor: Play the two openings. The groove is the same: the bass line, the tempo, the bouncing synth. But on 'It's Nasty' it is not the Tom Tom Club record. Sugar Hill's studio band played it again, so the bass is a little rounder and the drums a little heavier, and the Furious Five rap over it. Listen for how quickly a hook could travel in 1981 to 1982: from a Bahamas studio to a Sugar Hill record within a year, by being replayed rather than copied.

explanation: Grandmaster Flash and the Furious Five made a rap record over the music of 'Genius of Love' in 1982, less than a year after it came out. They did not copy the actual recording: Sugar Hill's own house band played the music again, which was how most rap records were made before samplers were common. It crosses from a rock band's rhythm section into the Bronx generation. 'Genius of Love' became one of the most reused hooks in hip-hop and R&B, through Mariah Carey's 'Fantasy' (1995) and Latto's 'Big Energy' (2021), which is why Tom Tom Club is on the map.
